subject: Clinicera — Eval kickoff & next steps for model fit
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.inference>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@clinicera.com>, Tom Randall <tom.randall@clinicera.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clinicera — Eval kickoff & next steps for model fit

Hi Ayesha / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can get your customer-specific evals running on Redwood: 

Summary of goals
- Primary objective: identify a model that meets Clinicera's triage intent classification (3-way: "urgent", "routine", "follow-up") with >92% precision on urgent class and low false negative rate.
- Secondary: evaluate summarization quality for visit notes (extractive + short abstractive summary) for downstream billing/QA.

What Redwood will run / recommend
- Initial model candidates: rw-med-1.3b (fast, lower-cost baseline), rw-chat-7b-instruct (balanced), rw-13b-q4f (higher accuracy, quantized). We'll also surface an instruction-tuned open model from our catalog for comparison.
- Eval plan: two runs — classification benchmark (your labeled holdout) and summarization scoring (ROUGE-1/2 + human blind review on 200 samples).

Data & artifact asks (what we need from Clinicera)
1) One JSONL sample file with up to 5k records (see attached clinicera_sample.jsonl). Each record should have: id, raw_text, label (for classification), visit_type, and optionally gold_summary. If labels are probabilistic, include confidence field.
2) A short prompt set (we attached prompt_set_v1.txt) with archetypal system messages we'd like tested.
3) Live point of contact for data pull & SSO access to the small GCS bucket if you want us to ingest directly.

Scoring & pass/fail criteria
- Classification: precision (urgent) >= 92%, recall (urgent) >= 88%, macro F1 >= 0.90.
- Summarization: ROUGE-1 >= 0.55 plus human acceptability >= 85% on the 200-sample review.
- Regression alerts: any model showing >5% drop in classification precision vs baseline will be flagged for review.

Estimated timeline and cost
- If we receive the sample JSONL by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-09), we can turn around an initial benchmark within 5 business days.
- Estimated compute: classification run (5k samples) ~ 8-12 GPU-hours depending on batch size; summarization run + human review ~ 10 GPU-hours + review time. We'll attach a detailed cost estimate in the MAP.

Attachments: clinicera_sample.jsonl (format example), prompt_set_v1.txt, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Next steps (action owners)
- Clinicera: share the sample JSONL or a GCS link (Ayesha) — due: 2026-12-09 EOD
- Redwood: prepare eval job configs and model seed prompts (Monica) — due: 2026-12-10
- Stakeholder sync: 30-min results review the week of 2026-12-15 (Sean to propose slots)

Let me know if any of this needs rewording. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if you want to walk through the sample file together.

Best,

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.g@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0132

Date: 2026-12-06T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clinicera — Eval kickoff & next steps for model fit

Thanks Sean — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we upload the sample: 

1) Label schema: our "urgent" flag is currently assigned by triage nurses and is fairly conservative. We can provide both label and nurse_confidence (0-1). Is that enough or would you prefer label provenance (e.g., "triage_nurse_v1") as a separate field?
2) For summarization, are we OK with mixed-length source notes (some visits are 2-3 paragraphs, others 800+ words)? Should we truncate?
3) Regarding the human review: do you supply raters or do we? If you supply, what's the process/turnaround?

We'll aim to upload a redacted 3k-record sample to the Drive link by 2026-12-09. Also looping in Tom to confirm procurement needs to be aware of any short-term test credits required.

Ayesha Khan
Clinical Ops Lead, Clinicera
ayesha.k@clinicera.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.inference>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@clinicera.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.inference>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-07T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clinicera — Eval kickoff & next steps for model fit

Hi Ayesha — quick answers and a recommended concrete runbook so you can validate against your internal processes.

1) Label provenance: please include a provenance string (e.g., "triage_nurse_v1") if available. We don't require it, but it helps interpret edge cases during error analysis. Nurse_confidence is perfect — we can use that to weight training/holdout if you want.

2) Source length & truncation: Leave notes as-is in the sample. For the production eval we'll include run profiles: short (<256 tokens), medium (256-1024), long (>1024). We'll run truncation experiments with context-window-aware batching.

3) Human review: Redwood provides the blind human review workflow as an add-on. For this pilot we recommend Redwood-managed raters to avoid labeling drift — turnaround ~3 business days for 200 samples. If you prefer to use internal raters, we can provide the review UI and rubric.

Recommended runbook (short)
- Data ingest: Clinicera uploads clinicera_sample.jsonl to the Drive folder. Errors & schema mismatches get a validation report within 2 hours of upload.
- Eval config: classification job (seed prompts + 3 prompting strategies), summarization job (2 prompt templates + extractive post-filter).
- Metrics we will compute automatically: precision/recall/F1 by class, confusion matrix, per-token cost, latency percentiles (p50/p95), ROUGE scores for summarization.
- Human review: 200-sample blind panel; results integrated into the eval dashboard with reviewer notes.

Cost & credentials
- We've provisioned 100 USD of test credits on your account for pilot runs. If you need incremental credits, procurement (Tom) can approve a short-term addendum — happy to provide an SOC 2 appendix if needed.

Small JSONL schema example (we will validate automatically):
- id (string)
- raw_text (string)
- label (string)
- nurse_confidence (number 0-1)
- visit_type (string)
- gold_summary (string, optional)
- provenance (string, optional)

I'll upload a template file to the Drive link and a minimal eval config in the eval console. If everything looks good we'll queue the first run when we have the sample.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.p@redwood.inference
